claim: The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard leaves all generated code on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets without `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`. The requirement asks for all generated code to be decorated. The guard is unnecessary: `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and it accepts class targets. Libraries targeting netstandard2.0, very common for MessagePack users, still have their coverage skewed. The README text added by this change wrongly states that the attribute is unavailable on those targets.

claim: This change removes `this.HashCollisionResistant = copyFrom.HashCollisionResistant;` from the MessagePackSecurity copy constructor, which is unrelated to the requirement. Every derived copy (Clone, `WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth`, and so on) now silently drops collision-resistant hashing. For example, `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(100)` returns an instance with `HashCollisionResistant == false`. That re-opens hash-flooding DoS for untrusted data, which contradicts the secure-by-default history recorded in L4.

claim: The `MessagePackSecurity` copy constructor no longer copies `HashCollisionResistant`. `Clone()` and every `With*` method build on that constructor. So `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.WithMaximumObjectGraphDepth(100)` silently returns an instance with `HashCollisionResistant == false`. Hashtable and dictionary formatters then use a non-collision-resistant comparer on untrusted input. This is a hash-flooding DoS regression and is unrelated to REQ-2297.
